2610.03713.title: What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation
2610.03713.paper_summary: Continual learning treats degradation on previously seen data as evidence of failure, a convention inherited from settings with a stationary prediction target, where a correct label remains correct indefinitely. World models do not satisfy this condition. Their prediction target is the environment, which changes, so knowledge that was accurate when acquired may later become false, and discarding it is required behavior rather than a defect. Non-stationary ground truth is well studied in the concept drift literature and in the temporal factuality of language models, but has not been formulated for world models, which are distinctive in that they also encode knowledge that must never be revised. We argue that continual world models require retention stratified by invariance timescale, separating invariants such as physics and object permanence, which must never be revised, from instance-level facts that should be revised as soon as the environment changes. Standard forgetting metrics cannot distinguish a world model that has correctly revised outdated knowledge from one that has suffered catastrophic forgetting, and consequently rank a frozen model highest, while existing physical-reasoning benchmarks evaluate only frozen checkpoints. We propose differential retention, which reports invariant regression testing across the adaptation stream jointly with revision latency, without aggregation.
2610.03713.paper_summary_zh: 持續學習將對先前見過的數據的退化視為失敗的證據，這是一種從具有靜態預測目標的環境中繼承的常規，其中正確的標籤無限期地保持正確。世界模型不符合這一條件。它們的預測目標是環境，而環境是會變化的，因此當知識在獲取時是準確的，後來可能會變得不正確，捨棄這些知識是必要的行為，而不是缺陷。非靜態的真實情況在概念漂移文獻和語言模型的時間事實性中得到了充分研究，但尚未為世界模型進行公式化，因為這些模型的特點在於它們還編碼了永遠不應修訂的知識。我們主張持續的世界模型需要按不變性時間尺度進行保留分層，將如物理學和物體持久性等不變量與應在環境變化後立即修訂的實例級事實分開。標準的遺忘度量無法區分正確修訂過時知識的世界模型與遭受災難性遺忘的模型，因此將凍結模型評為最高，而現有的物理推理基準僅評估凍結檢查點。我們提出了差異保留，該方法在適應流中報告不變回歸測試，並與修訂延遲一起進行，而不進行聚合。
